A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TREAD research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison; embedded-graphic matching distinguishes retained graphics from additions and removals.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-generation experiments, architectural comparisons and routing ablations in Section 4, plus guidance experiments and generated samples in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds LightningDiT/Mamba comparisons, dropout controls and appendix training-loss trajectories.

M1.justification: Training-only token routing, reinsertion, the reconstruction objective and full-token inference remain unchanged. Applying TREAD to additional backbones and introducing dropout comparators do not change the proposed procedure; row selection for sequential models already appears in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-256 and ImageNet-512 class-conditional generation and MS-COCO text-to-image generation. Specifying COCO 2014 and adding backbone/control configurations do not establish different dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LightningDiT and Mamba comparisons with and without TREAD. New Table 5b compares TLDrop and TLDropR against SiT-B/2 and TREAD; Table 6 explicitly adds the unrouted DiT-XL/2 baseline already reported elsewhere. Table 1's comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: New configurations include 675M-parameter LightningDiT at 80K iterations with batch size 1024 and 111M-parameter Mamba at 400K iterations with batch size 256. Table 5b introduces SiT controls applying token dropout across all layers or layers 2-8. Existing training, sampling and evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 5b tests long routes against repeated single-layer token bypasses, extending the existing routing ablations. New Appendix B/Figure S10 shows loss trajectories through 100K iterations and their relationship to route length and final FID, supplementing the retained Figure 6 correlations.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. Figure 6 retains its correlation statistics, while the added loss curves introduce no defined confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New baseline/TREAD FID pairs are 5.14/3.71 for LightningDiT and 69.39/61.17 for Mamba. Table 5b adds dropout results of 32.00 and 24.28 against the retained TREAD value of 15.98. Table 4's ImageNet-512 baseline entry changes from 62.8 to 62.88. Loss trajectories are added, v2's Figure S11 sample gallery is removed, and Table 1's headline results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The diffusion formulation and routed objective in Equations 1-5, and the appendix sampling/noise definitions in Equations 6-7, remain mathematically equivalent. Clarifying the routed-token subscript introduces no new definition, assumption, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain architecture-agnostic routing without additional parameters and simultaneous efficiency and generation-quality gains. The 14x/37x speedups and guided/unguided FIDs of 2.09/3.93 are unchanged; the added experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds the explanation that direct reuse encourages less washed-out intermediate features. Section 4.3 and Appendix B interpret the loss gap through routing-induced training difficulty and use dropout controls to emphasize route configuration. Existing guidance, selection-rate, route-placement and mixed-precision qualifications are retained.

D1.justification: v3 identifies COCO 2014, explicitly extends row-selection guidance to Mamba, and documents sizes and budgets for added model configurations. The abstract replaces the direct code-repository link with a project-page link, without establishing changed resource availability. Appendix A retains its solver, VAE checkpoint, optimizer and fine-tuning details.

R1.justification: v3 adds Fuest et al.'s representation-learning survey and Yao et al.'s LightningDiT work while retaining its positioning against masking, pruning and learned routers. Finn et al.'s MAML reference is also added but incorrectly cited by the Mamba row in Table 2; Section 4.1 instead cites Gu and Dao.

P1.justification: Targeted editing condenses the first related-work subsection, adds descriptive paragraph headings in Section 3, and revises mechanism and ablation explanations. Author-affiliation and acknowledgement text also change. The main section sequence and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 gain batch-size columns and revised formatting; Table 5 becomes a two-part comparison. Figure S10 adds loss plots, the supplementary cover is merged with Appendix A, and v2's dog/butterfly/minivan gallery is removed. Remaining sample galleries and main figure graphics are retained, with caption, placement and numbering adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new dropout controls test the benefit of long routes more directly, while LightningDiT/Mamba comparisons strengthen architectural validation. Appendix B makes the existing loss argument easier to assess through training trajectories. These are useful but limited evidential gains over v2. The incorrect Mamba citation weakens traceability, but does not outweigh the added supporting evidence; the core method and headline findings remain stable.
